parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence; surviving sodomy provisions (limited to police/military) were struck down in 2024, and no documented targeting of trans visitors exists. No facility bans, no border friction documented, no organised targeting — the dossier's worst features are dated (2006 club closures, 2012 pride arrests) and aimed at visible LGBTQ activism, not trans travellers. However, the climate is strongly conservative: 69% favour criminalising same-sex relationships, religious bodies carry policy weight, there is no discrimination protection in any visitor-facing sector, no hate-crime provision is documented, and no tradition of gender-diverse acceptance appears. Under rule 13, a thin dossier with no criminalisation but strong documented social hostility, zero protective machinery, and no embedded acceptance resolves below the acceptance-with-protections tier (0.65–0.75) but above jurisdictions with enforced targeting. Recourse is thin: the traveller outed faces discrimination with no remedy, but not state prosecution. This sits in the upper elevated band, around the 0.55 anchors — no universal unremedied exclusion, but recurring hostility with incomplete protection and open questions (custody placement, ward practice) unresolved.
